name: google-calendar

service_account_key.description: Contents of a Google service account JSON key. Recommended over OAuth: it never expires. Share each calendar with the service account's email.

client_id.description: OAuth 2.0 client ID from Google Cloud Console. Not needed when service_account_key is set.

client_secret.description: OAuth 2.0 client secret from Google Cloud Console. Not needed when service_account_key is set.

refresh_token.description: OAuth 2.0 refresh token obtained via the authorization flow. Not needed when service_account_key is set.

calendar_id.description: Google Calendar ID to operate on. Use "primary" to target the user's main calendar.

ics_feeds.description: Optional read-only iCal feeds, as a JSON object mapping a calendar name to its .ics URL. Use this for calendars that can't be shared with a service account, such as calendars subscribed to by URL. They appear in list_calendars with calendar_id "ics:<name>".

instructions:
Setup instructions for google-calendar plugin

1. Create a Google Cloud project
   - Go to https://console.cloud.google.com/
   - Create a new project or select an existing one.

2. Enable the Google Calendar API
   - In the project, go to APIs & Services > Library.
   - Search for "Google Calendar API" and click Enable.

3. Create OAuth 2.0 credentials
   - Go to APIs & Services > Credentials.
   - Click "Create Credentials" > "OAuth client ID".
   - Choose application type: Desktop app.
   - Note the client_id and client_secret shown.

4. Authenticate

   Recommended: create a service account (IAM & Admin > Service Accounts > Keys > Add key > JSON), share each calendar with its email ("Make changes to events"), put the JSON key's contents in service_account_key, and set calendar_id to your calendar's ID (not "primary"). Service accounts never expire, unlike OAuth refresh tokens in "Testing" status (7 days), but can't invite attendees on personal Google accounts.

   Alternative: obtain an OAuth refresh token as follows.

   Tell Stavrobot your client_id and client_secret. Stavrobot will generate an authorization URL and give it to you.

   Open the URL in your browser, log in with your Google account, and click "Allow" to grant calendar access. Google will then display an authorization code on the page — copy it and paste it back to Stavrobot.

   Stavrobot will exchange the code for tokens and extract the refresh_token for you.

5. Set calendar_id

   Use "primary" to target your main Google Calendar, or find a specific calendar ID in Google Calendar settings under each calendar's details page.

6. Optional: iCal feeds

   Calendars you subscribed to by URL can't be shared with a service account. Set ics_feeds to a JSON object mapping a name to each feed's .ics URL (e.g. {"Rental": "https://example.com/calendar.ics"}). They are read-only and appear in list_calendars as "ics:<name>".
